claim: BMP7/BMP2 or BMP7/BMP4 heterodimers are more active than homodimers in vitro.
source: BMP7/BMP2 or BMP7/BMP4 heterodimers are more active than homodimers in vitro, but it is not known whether these heterodimers signal in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research and established scientific knowledge about BMP heterodimer activity in vitro.

claim: It is not known whether BMP7/BMP2 or BMP7/BMP4 heterodimers signal in vivo.
source: BMP7/BMP2 or BMP7/BMP4 heterodimers are more active than homodimers in vitro, but it is not known whether these heterodimers signal in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: A Bmp7R-GFlag mutation prevents proteolytic activation of the dimerized BMP7 precursor protein.
source: To test this, we generated knock in mice carrying a mutation (Bmp7R-GFlag) that prevents proteolytic activation of the dimerized BMP7 precursor protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental design and the genetic engineering approach described.

claim: The Bmp7R-GFlag mutation eliminates the function of BMP7 homodimers and all other BMPs that normally heterodimerize with BMP7.
source: This mutation eliminates the function of BMP7 homodimers and all other BMPs that normally heterodimerize with BMP7.
evidence: This is inferred from the mechanism of the cleavage mutation and its predicted effects on BMP function.

claim: Bmp7 null homozygotes are live born.
source: While Bmp7 null homozygotes are live born, Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes are embryonic lethal and have broadly reduced BMP activity.
evidence: This is supported by observational data from mouse breeding experiments.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes are embryonic lethal.
source: While Bmp7 null homozygotes are live born, Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes are embryonic lethal and have broadly reduced BMP activity.
evidence: This is supported by observational data from mouse breeding experiments shown in Table 3.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes have broadly reduced BMP activity.
source: While Bmp7 null homozygotes are live born, Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes are embryonic lethal and have broadly reduced BMP activity.
evidence: This is supported by BRE-LacZ reporter assays and pSmad immunostaining data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Compound heterozygotes carrying the Bmp7R-G allele together with a null allele of Bmp2 die during embryogenesis with defects in ventral body wall closure and/or the heart.
source: Furthermore, compound heterozygotes carrying the Bmp7R-G allele together with a null allele of Bmp2 or Bmp4 die during embryogenesis with defects in ventral body wall closure and/or the heart.
evidence: This is supported by observational data from breeding experiments and phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 5 and Table 4.

claim: Compound heterozygotes carrying the Bmp7R-G allele together with a null allele of Bmp4 die during embryogenesis with defects in ventral body wall closure and/or the heart.
source: Furthermore, compound heterozygotes carrying the Bmp7R-G allele together with a null allele of Bmp2 or Bmp4 die during embryogenesis with defects in ventral body wall closure and/or the heart.
evidence: This is supported by observational data from breeding experiments and phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 5 and Table 5.

claim: Endogenous BMP4/7 heterodimers exist.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation assays confirm that endogenous BMP4/7 heterodimers exist.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: BMP7 functions predominantly as a heterodimer with BMP2 or BMP4 during mammalian development.
source: Thus, BMP7 functions predominantly as a heterodimer with BMP2 or BMP4 during mammalian development, which may explain why mutations in either Bmp4 or Bmp7 lead to a similar spectrum of congenital defects in humans.
evidence: This is inferred from the genetic and biochemical data presented throughout the study.

claim: Mutations in either Bmp4 or Bmp7 lead to a similar spectrum of congenital defects in humans.
source: Thus, BMP7 functions predominantly as a heterodimer with BMP2 or BMP4 during mammalian development, which may explain why mutations in either Bmp4 or Bmp7 lead to a similar spectrum of congenital defects in humans.
evidence: This is supported by citations to human genetic studies.

claim: BMPs were initially discovered as bone inducing factors.
source: Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) are secreted molecules that were initially discovered as bone inducing factors and were subsequently shown to play numerous critical roles during embryogenesis (Bragdon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: BMPs play numerous critical roles during embryogenesis.
source: Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) are secreted molecules that were initially discovered as bone inducing factors and were subsequently shown to play numerous critical roles during embryogenesis (Bragdon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Recombinant BMPs are used clinically to treat bone loss caused by trauma or disease.
source: Recombinant BMPs are used clinically to treat bone loss caused by trauma or disease, but their usefulness as osteoinductive agents is limited by a short half-life when implanted in vivo (Khan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The usefulness of recombinant BMPs as osteoinductive agents is limited by a short half-life when implanted in vivo.
source: Recombinant BMPs are used clinically to treat bone loss caused by trauma or disease, but their usefulness as osteoinductive agents is limited by a short half-life when implanted in vivo (Khan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: BMPs are grouped into subfamilies based on sequence similarity.
source: BMPs are grouped into subfamilies based on sequence similarity, and can signal as either homodimers or as heterodimers.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about BMP classification.

claim: BMPs can signal as either homodimers or as heterodimers.
source: BMPs are grouped into subfamilies based on sequence similarity, and can signal as either homodimers or as heterodimers.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about BMP signaling.

claim: Class I BMPs consist of BMP2 and BMP4.
source: The class I BMPs, BMP2 and BMP4, can heterodimerize with class II BMPs, consisting of BMPs 5–8 (Guo and Wu, 2012).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Class II BMPs consist of BMPs 5-8.
source: The class I BMPs, BMP2 and BMP4, can heterodimerize with class II BMPs, consisting of BMPs 5–8 (Guo and Wu, 2012).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Class I BMPs can heterodimerize with class II BMPs.
source: The class I BMPs, BMP2 and BMP4, can heterodimerize with class II BMPs, consisting of BMPs 5–8 (Guo and Wu, 2012).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Heterodimers composed of class I and class II BMPs show a higher specific activity than do homodimers.
source: Heterodimers composed of class I and class II BMPs show a higher specific activity than do homodimers.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: BMP2/7 or BMP4/7 heterodimers are significantly more potent than any homodimer in osteogenic differentiation assays.
source: For example, homodimers of BMP2, −4, or-7 can all induce bone formation, but BMP2/7 or BMP4/7 heterodimers are significantly more potent than any homodimer in osteogenic differentiation assays (Aono et al., 1995; Kaito et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: BMP2/6 heterodimers show enhanced ability to activate downstream signaling in embryonic stem cells.
source: Likewise, BMP2/6 heterodimers show enhanced ability to activate downstream signaling in embryonic stem cells (Valera et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: BMP2/7 and BMP4/7 heterodimers show enhanced ability to induce ventral fate in Xenopus and zebrafish.
source: BMP2/7 and BMP4/7 heterodimers also show enhanced ability to induce ventral fate in Xenopus and zebrafish (Nishimatsu and Thomsen, 1998; Schmid et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Whether endogenous BMPs function primarily as homodimers or heterodimers in vivo remains controversial.
source: While it is widely accepted that recombinant class I/II BMP heterodimers have higher specific activity than homodimers, whether endogenous BMPs function primarily as homodimers or heterodimers in vivo remains controversial.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Mutations in either Bmp2b or Bmp7 lead to a complete loss of signaling in zebrafish embryos.
source: Mutations in either Bmp2b or Bmp7 lead to a complete loss of signaling in zebrafish embryos and this can be rescued by recombinant heterodimers, but not by either homodimer (Little and Mullins, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Loss of signaling in zebrafish embryos with Bmp2b or Bmp7 mutations can be rescued by recombinant heterodimers, but not by either homodimer.
source: Mutations in either Bmp2b or Bmp7 lead to a complete loss of signaling in zebrafish embryos and this can be rescued by recombinant heterodimers, but not by either homodimer (Little and Mullins, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: An ectopically expressed epitope-tagged form of BMP2b pulls down endogenous BMP7 and vice versa in zebrafish.
source: In addition, an ectopically expressed epitope-tagged form of BMP2b pulls down endogenous BMP7 and vice versa (Little and Mullins, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: BMP2/7 heterodimers are essential to establish the dorsoventral axis in fish.
source: Thus, BMP2/7 heterodimers are essential to establish the dorsoventral axis in fish.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited zebrafish studies.

claim: DPP is not properly localized to the embryonic midline in Drosophila in the absence of SCREW.
source: In Drosophila, DPP (the fly homolog of BMP2/4) is not properly localized to the embryonic midline in the absence of SCREW (a BMP7 homolog) and this is proposed to be due to preferential transport of DPP/SCREW heterodimers (Shimmi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Expression of DPP and SCREW homodimers in distinct regions of the Drosophila embryo can activate BMP signaling at levels equivalent to the heterodimer.
source: However, expression of DPP and SCREW homodimers in distinct regions of the embryo can activate BMP signaling at levels equivalent to the heterodimer (Nguyen et al., 1998; Wang and Ferguson, 2005), suggesting that homodimers are sufficient for development.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Evidence that class I/II BMP heterodimers exist or are required for mammalian development is lacking.
source: Evidence that class I/II BMP heterodimers exist or are required for mammalian development is lacking.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: Bmp4 null homozygotes die during early development with defects in multiple tissues that correlate well with their respective expression domains.
source: Bmp4 or Bmp2 null homozygotes die during early development with defects in multiple tissues that correlate well with their respective expression domains (Winnier et al., 1995; Zhang and Bradley, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bmp2 null homozygotes die during early development with defects in multiple tissues that correlate well with their respective expression domains.
source: Bmp4 or Bmp2 null homozygotes die during early development with defects in multiple tissues that correlate well with their respective expression domains (Winnier et al., 1995; Zhang and Bradley, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bmp8 is restricted to the developing testes and placenta.
source: Among Class II BMPs, Bmp8 is restricted to the developing testes and placenta while Bmp5, Bmp6 and Bmp7 are broadly expressed throughout embryogenesis (Zhao, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Bmp5, Bmp6 and Bmp7 are broadly expressed throughout embryogenesis.
source: Among Class II BMPs, Bmp8 is restricted to the developing testes and placenta while Bmp5, Bmp6 and Bmp7 are broadly expressed throughout embryogenesis (Zhao, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Mice homozygous for null mutations in any single Class II Bmp gene survive embryogenesis.
source: Mice homozygous for null mutations in any single Class II Bmp gene survive embryogenesis (King et al., 1994; Dudley et al., 1995; Luo et al., 1995; Solloway et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bmp5;Bmp7 double mutants are embryonic lethal.
source: By contrast, Bmp5;Bmp7 or Bmp6;Bmp7 double mutants are embryonic lethal (Solloway and Robertson, 1999; Kim et al., 2001), demonstrating functional redundancy.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bmp6;Bmp7 double mutants are embryonic lethal.
source: By contrast, Bmp5;Bmp7 or Bmp6;Bmp7 double mutants are embryonic lethal (Solloway and Robertson, 1999; Kim et al., 2001), demonstrating functional redundancy.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bmp2/7 and Bmp4/7 double heterozygotes present with no abnormalities or minor skeletal abnormalities.
source: Bmp2/7 and Bmp4/7 double heterozygotes present with no abnormalities or minor skeletal abnormalities (Katagiri et al., 1998), raising the possibility that heterodimers are not required for early mammalian development.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: All BMPs are generated as inactive precursor proteins that dimerize and fold within the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: All BMPs are generated as inactive precursor proteins that dimerize and fold within the endoplasmic reticulum (Bragdon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The BMP precursor protein is cleaved by members of the proprotein convertase (PC) family to generate the active, disulfide bonded ligand along with two prodomain fragments.
source: The precursor protein is then cleaved by members of the proprotein convertase (PC) family to generate the active, disulfide bonded ligand along with two prodomain fragments.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: BMP4 and BMP7 preferentially form heterodimers rather than either homodimer when ectopically coexpressed in Xenopus embryos.
source: We have shown that BMP4 and BMP7 preferentially form heterodimers rather than either homodimer when ectopically coexpressed in Xenopus embryos (Neugebauer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Bmp4 and Bmp7 show overlapping patterns of expression in many tissues.
source: Bmp4 and Bmp7 show overlapping patterns of expression in many tissues (Danesh et al., 2009), suggesting that they may form heterodimers in some contexts.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Heterozygous mutations in either Bmp4 or Bmp7 are associated with a similar spectrum of ocular, brain and palate abnormalities in humans.
source: In humans, heterozygous mutations in either Bmp4 or Bmp7 are associated with a similar spectrum of ocular, brain and palate abnormalities (Bakrania et al., 2008; Suzuki et al., 2009; Wyatt et al., 2010; Reis et al., 2011), consistent with the possibility that mutations in either gene lead to reduced BMP4/7 heterodimer activity.
evidence: This is supported by citations to human genetic studies.

claim: BMPs carrying mutations in the PC cleavage motif form inactive dimers with wild type proteins.
source: BMPs carrying mutations in the PC cleavage motif form inactive dimers with wild type proteins.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cleavage mutant forms of BMP7 dominantly interfere with both BMP7 and BMP4 signaling when overexpressed in Xenopus.
source: For example, cleavage mutant forms of BMP7 dominantly interfere with both BMP7 and BMP4 signaling when overexpressed in Xenopus (Hawley et al., 1995; Nishimatsu and Thomsen, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A mouse carrying a point mutation in the cleavage site of BMP5 has more severe skeletal abnormalities than Bmp5 homozygous null mutants.
source: A mouse carrying a point mutation in the cleavage site of the type II BMP, BMP5, has more severe skeletal abnormalities than Bmp5 homozygous null mutants (Ho et al., 2008), consistent with the possibility that it interferes with Class I heterodimeric partners, but this has not been explored.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Endogenous heterodimers containing BMP7 exist in vivo.
source: In the current studies, we used genetic and biochemical analysis to test the hypothesis that endogenous heterodimers containing BMP7 exist in vivo. We show that endogenous heterodimers do form in vivo, and are the predominant functional ligand in many if not all tissues of developing mouse embryos.
evidence: This is supported by the genetic and biochemical data presented in the study.

claim: Endogenous BMP7-containing heterodimers are the predominant functional ligand in many if not all tissues of developing mouse embryos.
source: We show that endogenous heterodimers do form in vivo, and are the predominant functional ligand in many if not all tissues of developing mouse embryos.
evidence: This is supported by the genetic and phenotypic data presented in the study.

claim: Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos were recovered at the predicted Mendelian frequency throughout development.
source: Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos were recovered at the predicted Mendelian frequency throughout development and were adult viable with no apparent defects (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 1.

claim: Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos were adult viable with no apparent defects.
source: Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos were recovered at the predicted Mendelian frequency throughout development and were adult viable with no apparent defects (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 1.

claim: Bmp7 null homozygotes were recovered at the predicted Mendelian ratio between embryonic day (E)9.5 and E18.5.
source: Bmp7 null homozygotes were recovered at the predicted Mendelian ratio between embryonic day (E)9.5 and E18.5 (Table 2) but died shortly after birth.
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 2.

claim: Bmp7 null homozygotes died shortly after birth.
source: Bmp7 null homozygotes were recovered at the predicted Mendelian ratio between embryonic day (E)9.5 and E18.5 (Table 2) but died shortly after birth.
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 2.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mice were present at the predicted Mendelian frequency through E11.5.
source: By contrast, Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mice were present at the predicted Mendelian frequency through E11.5 but were not recovered after this stage (Table 3).
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 3.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mice were not recovered after E11.5.
source: By contrast, Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mice were present at the predicted Mendelian frequency through E11.5 but were not recovered after this stage (Table 3).
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 3.

claim: Bmp7Flag/Flag and Bmp7-/- embryos were indistinguishable from wild type littermates at E9.5–11.5, with the exception of slightly smaller eyes in 25% of the Bmp7-/- embryos examined at E11.5.
source: Bmp7Flag/Flag (Figure 1D,D', G,G', J,J') and Bmp7-/- (Figure 1F,F', I,I', L,L') embryos were indistinguishable from wild type littermates at E9.5–11.5, with the exception of slightly smaller eyes in 25% of the Bmp7-/- embryos examined at E11.5 (n = 7; Figure 1L,L').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 1.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes appeared grossly normal but were slightly smaller than age matched wild type littermates at E9.5.
source: Bmp7R-GFlag/ R-GFlag embryos appeared grossly normal but were slightly smaller than age matched (by somite number) wild type littermates at E9.5 (n = 45; Figure 1E,E').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 1.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes were smaller and had smaller limb buds than littermates at E10.5.
source: Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes were smaller, and had smaller limb buds than littermates at E10.5 (n = 13; Figure 1H,H', Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and were resorbing at E11.5 (n = 12; Figure 1K,K').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes were resorbing at E11.5.
source: Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes were smaller, and had smaller limb buds than littermates at E10.5 (n = 13; Figure 1H,H', Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and were resorbing at E11.5 (n = 12; Figure 1K,K').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 1.

claim: All Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes showed multiple abnormalities at E10.5 including smaller and less distinct forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain, pericardial edema, smaller limb buds and no eye.
source: All Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes showed multiple abnormalities at E10.5 (Figure 1H,H') including smaller and less distinct forebrain (fb), midbrain (mb) and hindbrain (hb), pericardial edema (arrows), smaller limb buds (flb) and no eye (e).
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 1.

claim: Expression of wild type levels of an uncleavable BMP7 precursor protein leads to earlier lethality and more severe phenotypic defects than does complete absence of BMP7 protein.
source: Thus, expression of wild type levels of an uncleavable BMP7 precursor protein leads to earlier lethality and more severe phenotypic defects than does complete absence of BMP7 protein, suggesting that endogenous BMP7-containing heterodimers perform essential functions during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparative phenotypic analysis of Bmp7R-GFlag and Bmp7 null mutants.

claim: Endogenous BMP7-containing heterodimers perform essential functions during early embryogenesis.
source: Thus, expression of wild type levels of an uncleavable BMP7 precursor protein leads to earlier lethality and more severe phenotypic defects than does complete absence of BMP7 protein, suggesting that endogenous BMP7-containing heterodimers perform essential functions during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparative phenotypic analysis.

claim: 23% of Bmp7R-GFlag heterozygotes showed runting, microphthalmia and/or anophthalmia as early as E14.5.
source: Bmp7R-GFlag heterozygotes were adult viable (Supplementary file 1), but 23% showed runting, microphthalmia and/or anophthalmia as early as E14.5 (n = 13, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B) that persisted into adulthood (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E–F).
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Eye defects in Bmp7R-GFlag heterozygotes persisted into adulthood.
source: Bmp7R-GFlag heterozygotes were adult viable (Supplementary file 1), but 23% showed runting, microphthalmia and/or anophthalmia as early as E14.5 (n = 13, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B) that persisted into adulthood (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E–F).
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Eye defects were never observed in Bmp7 null heterozygotes.
source: These defects were never observed in Bmp7 null heterozygotes (n = 8; Figure 1—figure supplement 3C) although one or both eyes were absent in late gestation Bmp7 null homozygotes (n = 5; Figure 1—figure supplement 3D) as previously reported (Dudley et al., 1995; Luo et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: One or both eyes were absent in late gestation Bmp7 null homozygotes.
source: These defects were never observed in Bmp7 null heterozygotes (n = 8; Figure 1—figure supplement 3C) although one or both eyes were absent in late gestation Bmp7 null homozygotes (n = 5; Figure 1—figure supplement 3D) as previously reported (Dudley et al., 1995; Luo et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by observational data, images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and citations to prior research.

claim: The fibula was shortened and failed to articulate with the knee in 13% of Bmp7R-GFlag heterozygotes.
source: Skeletal analysis revealed that the fibula was shortened and failed to articulate with the knee in 13% of Bmp7R-GFlag heterozygotes that were analyzed (n = 14; Figure 1—figure supplement 3G,H).
evidence: This is supported by skeletal preparation data and images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The fibula defect has been observed in mice in which both Bmp2 and Bmp7 are conditionally deleted from the limbs, but not in mice lacking any single BMP family member.
source: This defect has been observed in mice in which both Bmp2 and Bmp7 are conditionally deleted from the limbs, but not in mice lacking any single BMP family member (Bandyopadhyay et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The BMP7R-GFlag precursor protein dominantly sequesters endogenous class I BMPs in non-functional dimers.
source: These findings support a model in which the BMP7R-GFlag precursor protein dominantly sequesters endogenous class I BMPs in non-functional dimers.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic data in Bmp7R-GFlag heterozygotes.

claim: Bmp2, 4, and 7 are expressed in overlapping domains of the developing heart.
source: Bmp2, 4, and 7 are expressed in overlapping domains of the developing heart (Dudley and Robertson, 1997; Danesh et al., 2009), raising the possibility that heart defects cause embryonic lethality in Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: At E10.5, hearts dissected from Bmp7Flag and Bmp7 null homozygotes were indistinguishable from wild type littermates with morphologically distinguishable atria, ventricles, and outflow tract.
source: At E10.5, hearts dissected from Bmp7Flag (n = 5) and Bmp7 null homozygotes (n = 6) were indistinguishable from wild type littermates with morphologically distinguishable atria, ventricles, and outflow tract (OFT) (Figure 2A–A', C–C').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 2.

claim: All hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos at E10.5 appeared to have thinner walls, had a common atrium, a smaller right ventricle and a small, malformed OFT relative to wild type littermates.
source: By contrast, all hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos (n = 6) appeared to have thinner walls, had a common atrium, a smaller right ventricle and a small, malformed OFT relative to wild type littermates (Figure 2B–B').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 2.

claim: Hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants were morphologically normal at E9.5.
source: In addition, although hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants were morphologically normal at E9.5, expression of the direct BMP target gene, Nkx2.5 (Lien et al., 2002), was severely reduced in all hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants relative to littermates at E9.5 (n = 10) and E10.5 (n = 6) (Figure 2E–E', H–H', K–K', N–N').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 2.

claim: Expression of Nkx2.5 was severely reduced in all hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants relative to littermates at E9.5 and E10.5.
source: In addition, although hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants were morphologically normal at E9.5, expression of the direct BMP target gene, Nkx2.5 (Lien et al., 2002), was severely reduced in all hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants relative to littermates at E9.5 (n = 10) and E10.5 (n = 6) (Figure 2E–E', H–H', K–K', N–N').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data and images shown in Figure 2.

claim: Nkx2.5 is a direct BMP target gene.
source: In addition, although hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants were morphologically normal at E9.5, expression of the direct BMP target gene, Nkx2.5 (Lien et al., 2002), was severely reduced in all hearts of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag mutants relative to littermates at E9.5 (n = 10) and E10.5 (n = 6) (Figure 2E–E', H–H', K–K', N–N').
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: No differences were detected in expression of Nkx2.5 in Bmp7Flag or Bmp7 null homozygotes relative to wild type littermates.
source: No differences were detected in expression of Nkx2.5 in Bmp7Flag (Figure 2D–D', G–G', J–J', M–M') or in Bmp7 null homozygotes (Figure 2F–F', I–I', L–L', O–O') relative to wild type littermates.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data and images shown in Figure 2.

claim: The BRE:LacZ transgene contains a BMP-responsive element coupled to LacZ, which serves as an in vivo reporter of BMP signaling downstream of all endogenous BMP ligands.
source: This transgene contains a BMP-responsive element coupled to LacZ, which serves as an in vivo reporter of BMP signaling downstream of all endogenous BMP ligands (Monteiro et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: X-GAL staining for ß-galactosidase activity in Bmp7+/+;BRE:LacZ embryos revealed strong endogenous BMP activity in the brain, eye, branchial arches, heart, and ventroposterior mesoderm at E9.5.
source: X-GAL staining for ß-galactosidase activity in Bmp7+/+;BRE:LacZ embryos revealed strong endogenous BMP activity in the brain, eye, branchial arches (BA), heart, and ventroposterior mesoderm (VPM) (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is supported by X-GAL staining data and images shown in Figure 3.

claim: No differences in BMP activity were detected in any tissues in Bmp7-/- embryos at E9.5.
source: No differences in BMP activity were detected in any of these tissues in Bmp7-/- embryos (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by X-GAL staining data and images shown in Figure 3.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos exhibited a reproducible reduction in BMP activity in the brain, ventroposterior mesoderm, and heart at E9.5.
source: By contrast, as shown in Figure 3C and D, Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos exhibited a reproducible reduction in BMP activity in the brain, ventroposterior mesoderm, and heart.
evidence: This is supported by X-GAL staining data and images shown in Figure 3.

claim: The reduction in BMP activity in the heart of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos was most pronounced in the right ventricle and the OFT.
source: The reduction in staining in the heart of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos was most pronounced in the right ventricle (outlined in white in the inset) and the OFT (outlined in magenta in inset).
evidence: This is supported by X-GAL staining data and images shown in Figure 3.

claim: BMP activity staining was completely absent in the eye of Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos at E9.5.
source: In addition, staining was completely absent in the eye (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by X-GAL staining data and images shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mice expressing endogenous levels of an uncleavable form of the BMP7 precursor protein show widespread loss of BMP activity that is not observed in mice lacking BMP7 protein.
source: Thus, mice expressing endogenous levels of an uncleavable form of the BMP7 precursor protein show widespread loss of BMP activity that is not observed in mice lacking BMP7 protein.
evidence: This is inferred from the BRE-LacZ reporter data comparing Bmp7R-GFlag and Bmp7 null mutants.

claim: Bmp2, 4 and 7 are co-expressed in the dorsal surface ectoderm overlying the spinal cord by E8.
source: Bmp2, 4 and 7 are co-expressed in the dorsal surface ectoderm overlying the spinal cord by E8 (Solloway and Robertson, 1999; Danesh et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: BMP signaling from the ectoderm is required for induction of the roof plate at E9.
source: BMP signaling from the ectoderm is required for induction of the roof plate at E9, and BMPs and other factors secreted from the roof plate are subsequently required for specification, migration and axon guidance of dorsal interneurons (Chizhikov and Millen, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: BMPs and other factors secreted from the roof plate are required for specification, migration and axon guidance of dorsal interneurons.
source: BMP signaling from the ectoderm is required for induction of the roof plate at E9, and BMPs and other factors secreted from the roof plate are subsequently required for specification, migration and axon guidance of dorsal interneurons (Chizhikov and Millen, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Levels of pSmad1/5/8 were unchanged in the roof plate of Bmp7-/- and Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos relative to wild type littermates at E9.5.
source: Levels of pSmad1/5/8 were unchanged in the roof plate of Bmp7-/- (Figure 3E–F) and Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos relative to wild type littermates (Figure 3I–J), but were severely reduced in the roof plate of Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes (Figure 3G–H).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data and images shown in Figure 3.

claim: Levels of pSmad1/5/8 were severely reduced in the roof plate of Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes at E9.5.
source: Levels of pSmad1/5/8 were unchanged in the roof plate of Bmp7-/- (Figure 3E–F) and Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos relative to wild type littermates (Figure 3I–J), but were severely reduced in the roof plate of Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes (Figure 3G–H).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data and images shown in Figure 3.

claim: Expression of lmx1a is induced in the nascent roof plate downstream of BMP signaling from the epidermal ectoderm.
source: Expression of lmx1a is induced in the nascent roof plate downstream of BMP signaling from the epidermal ectoderm, and is the major mediator of BMP signaling in the dorsal neural tube (Chizhikov and Millen, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: lmx1a is the major mediator of BMP signaling in the dorsal neural tube.
source: Expression of lmx1a is induced in the nascent roof plate downstream of BMP signaling from the epidermal ectoderm, and is the major mediator of BMP signaling in the dorsal neural tube (Chizhikov and Millen, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Expression of lmx1a was reduced by 50% in all E9.5 Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos.
source: Expression of lmx1a was reduced by 50% in all E9.5 Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag embryos that were examined (n = 3; Figure 3K–O).
evidence: This is supported by in situ HCR data and images shown in Figure 3.

claim: BMP7 containing heterodimers secreted from the epidermal ectoderm are major contributors to roof plate induction.
source: Thus, BMP7 containing heterodimers secreted from the epidermal ectoderm are major contributors to roof plate induction.
evidence: This is inferred from the lmx1a expression data in Bmp7R-GFlag mutants.

claim: Cells incubated with BMP7R-GFlag showed the same barely detectable level of immunoreactive pSmad1/5/8 as did control cells.
source: Cells incubated with BMP7R-GFlag showed the same barely detectable level of immunoreactive pSmad1/5/8 as did control cells (Figure 4B, compare lane 1 and 3), indicating that the precursor protein lacks activity.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The BMP7R-GFlag precursor protein lacks activity.
source: Cells incubated with BMP7R-GFlag showed the same barely detectable level of immunoreactive pSmad1/5/8 as did control cells (Figure 4B, compare lane 1 and 3), indicating that the precursor protein lacks activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the pSmad1/5/8 immunoblot data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Levels of pSmad1/5/8 were elevated to the same extent in cells incubated with BMP4 alone, or with BMP4 and BMP7R-GFlag together.
source: Levels of pSmad1/5/8 were elevated to the same extent in cells incubated with BMP4 alone, or with BMP4 and BMP7R-GFlag together (compare lane 2 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Uncleaved BMP7R-GFlag precursor protein homodimers cannot act outside of the cell to block the ability of BMP4 to signal.
source: Thus, uncleaved BMP7R-GFlag precursor protein homodimers cannot act outside of the cell to block the ability of BMP4 to signal.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell culture experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: When BMP4 and BMP7R-GFlag were co-expressed, relatively equivalent amounts of cleaved, mature BMP4 were detected in Flag immunoprecipitates and in input samples.
source: When BMP4 and BM7R-GFlag were co-expressed, relatively equivalent amounts of cleaved, mature BMP4 were detected in Flag immunoprecipitates and in input samples, suggesting that most BMP4 was heterodimerized with BMP7R-GFlag (Figure 4D, compare lanes 3 and 6).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblot data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Most BMP4 was heterodimerized with BMP7R-GFlag when co-expressed.
source: When BMP4 and BM7R-GFlag were co-expressed, relatively equivalent amounts of cleaved, mature BMP4 were detected in Flag immunoprecipitates and in input samples, suggesting that most BMP4 was heterodimerized with BMP7R-GFlag (Figure 4D, compare lanes 3 and 6).
evidence: This is inferred from the immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Steady state levels of mature BMP4 protein were much higher in the media of cells cotransfected with BMP4 and BMP7R-GFlag DNA than in an equivalent volume of media from cells transfected with the same amount of BMP4 DNA alone.
source: Steady state levels of mature BMP4 protein were much higher in the media of cells cotransfected with BMP4 and BMP7R-GFlag DNA than in an equivalent volume of media from cells transfected with the same amount of BMP4 DNA alone (compare lanes 2 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4.

claim: BMP4/BMP7R-GFlag heterodimers accumulate to much higher levels than do BMP4 homodimers.
source: The finding that BMP4/BMP7R-GFlag heterodimers accumulate to much higher levels than do BMP4 homodimers is consistent with an inability of the heterodimer to bind to, and induce internalization and degradation of the ligand/receptor complex, a process that is critical for normal embryogenesis (Aoyama et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from the immunoblot data and supported by citation to prior research on receptor-mediated degradation.

claim: Internalization and degradation of the ligand/receptor complex is critical for normal embryogenesis.
source: The finding that BMP4/BMP7R-GFlag heterodimers accumulate to much higher levels than do BMP4 homodimers is consistent with an inability of the heterodimer to bind to, and induce internalization and degradation of the ligand/receptor complex, a process that is critical for normal embryogenesis (Aoyama et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: When untransfected HEK293T cells were exposed to media containing BMP4 homodimers, pSmad1 levels were increased 10-fold over basal levels.
source: When untransfected HEK293T cells were exposed to media containing BMP4 homodimers, pSmad1 levels were increased 10-fold over basal levels (compare lanes 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Exposure to media from cells co-transfected with BMP4 and BMP7R-GFlag led to a 3.4-fold elevation of pSmad1 levels.
source: By contrast, exposure to the same volume of media from cells co-transfected with BMP4 and BMP7R-GFlag led to a 3.4-fold elevation of pSmad1 levels (compare lane 1 and 3), despite the fact that this media contains very high levels of cleaved BMP4 heterodimerized with BMP7R-GFlag.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The BMP4 precursor protein is cleaved and secreted when heterodimerized with the uncleavable BMP7R-GFlag precursor.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that the BMP4 precursor protein is cleaved and secreted when heterodimerized with the uncleavable BMP7R-GFlag precursor.
evidence: This is inferred from the immunoblot and immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4.

claim: BMP4/BMP7R-GFlag heterodimers are less able, or unable to bind and/or activate BMP receptors.
source: However, this cleavage product is less able, or unable to bind and/or activate BMP receptors.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced pSmad1 activation despite high levels of BMP4 in the media.

claim: Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ mutants were present at the predicted Mendelian ratios at E15.5, but were not recovered at weaning.
source: When Bmp7R-GFlag/+ and Bmp2-/+ mice were intercrossed, Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ mutants were present at the predicted Mendelian ratios at E15.5, but were not recovered at weaning (Table 4).
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 4.

claim: Bmp2-/+ and Bmp7R-GFlag/+ mice were indistinguishable from wild type littermates at E14.5.
source: Bmp2-/+ and Bmp7R-GFlag/+ mice were indistinguishable from wild type littermates (Figure 5A–C), whereas all (n = 10) E14.5 Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos showed peripheral edema (Figure 5D–E,D'–E', arrowheads) along with defects in ventral body wall closure that ranged from umbilical hernia (Figure 5E, arrow, n = 4) to omphalocele, in which the liver and other visceral organs were externalized (Figure 5D,D', arrows, n = 6).
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: All E14.5 Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos showed peripheral edema.
source: Bmp2-/+ and Bmp7R-GFlag/+ mice were indistinguishable from wild type littermates (Figure 5A–C), whereas all (n = 10) E14.5 Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos showed peripheral edema (Figure 5D–E,D'–E', arrowheads) along with defects in ventral body wall closure that ranged from umbilical hernia (Figure 5E, arrow, n = 4) to omphalocele, in which the liver and other visceral organs were externalized (Figure 5D,D', arrows, n = 6).
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: E14.5 Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos showed defects in ventral body wall closure that ranged from umbilical hernia to omphalocele.
source: Bmp2-/+ and Bmp7R-GFlag/+ mice were indistinguishable from wild type littermates (Figure 5A–C), whereas all (n = 10) E14.5 Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos showed peripheral edema (Figure 5D–E,D'–E', arrowheads) along with defects in ventral body wall closure that ranged from umbilical hernia (Figure 5E, arrow, n = 4) to omphalocele, in which the liver and other visceral organs were externalized (Figure 5D,D', arrows, n = 6).
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: Six of the ten Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ compound heterozygotes were smaller than their littermates at E14.5.
source: In addition, six of the ten compound heterozygotes were smaller than their littermates (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: Out of four Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ hearts that were examined histologically, three showed ventricular septal defects.
source: Out of four Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ hearts that were examined histologically, three showed ventricular septal defects (VSDs) (Figure 5G',H', asterisks), and two showed defects in alignment of the aorta and pulmonary trunk (Figure 5G',H') relative to wild type or single mutant siblings (Figure 5F,F').
evidence: This is supported by histological data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: Two Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ hearts showed defects in alignment of the aorta and pulmonary trunk.
source: Out of four Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ hearts that were examined histologically, three showed ventricular septal defects (VSDs) (Figure 5G',H', asterisks), and two showed defects in alignment of the aorta and pulmonary trunk (Figure 5G',H') relative to wild type or single mutant siblings (Figure 5F,F').
evidence: This is supported by histological data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: In two Bmp2-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ compound mutants, the walls of the ventricles remained highly trabeculated and had not undergone compaction.
source: In two compound mutants, the walls of the ventricles remained highly trabeculated and had not undergone compaction (Figure 5G,G').
evidence: This is supported by histological data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: An identical spectrum of ventral body wall, OFT and ventricular septal defects is observed in Bmp2-/+;Bmp4-/+ compound mutants.
source: An identical spectrum of ventral body wall, OFT and ventricular septal defects is observed in Bmp2-/+;Bmp4-/+ compound mutants (Goldman et al., 2009; Uchimura et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bmp4-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ compound mutants were present at predicted Mendelian ratios at E9.5–11.5, but were not recovered at E12.5 or later.
source: To assess whether BMP4/7 heterodimers are required for development, we intercrossed Bmp7R-GFlag/+ and Bmp4-/+ mice. Compound mutants were present at predicted Mendelian ratios at E9.5–11.5, but were not recovered at E12.5 or later (Table 5).
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 5.

claim: Bmp4-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos appeared grossly normal at E9.5, and expression of the BMP target gene Nkx2.5 was intact in the heart.
source: Bmp4-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos appeared grossly normal at E9.5, and expression of the BMP target gene Nkx2.5 was intact in the heart (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–F').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: By E10.5 all eight Bmp4-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos that were examined were smaller than littermates and showed defects in heart development.
source: However, by E10.5 all eight embryos that were examined were smaller than littermates (Figure 5I–L) and showed defects in heart development (Figure 5I–L').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: Bmp4-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ hearts had a common atrium, and a smaller, malformed right ventricle and OFT at E10.5.
source: Specifically, whereas the hearts of wild type and single mutant siblings had morphologically distinguishable atria, ventricles, and OFT (Figure 5I'–K'), Bmp4-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ hearts had a common atrium (CA), and a smaller, malformed right ventricle and OFT (Figure 5L').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: Expression of Nkx2.5 was reduced in the hearts of all Bmp4-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos at E10.5.
source: In addition, expression of the BMP target gene Nkx2.5 was reduced in the hearts of all Bmp4-/+;Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos (Figure 5L') relative to littermates (Figure 5I'–K').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag/- mutants were present at predicted Mendelian ratios at E9.5–10.5 but were not recovered at E12.5 or later.
source: To test whether other class II BMPs can compensate for loss of BMP7 in the heterodimer pool in Bmp7R-GFlag heterozygotes, we intercrossed Bmp7R-GFlag/+ and Bmp7-/+ mice. Bmp7R-GFlag/- mutants were present at predicted Mendelian ratios at E9.5–10.5 but were not recovered at E12.5 or later (Table 6).
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Table 6.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag/- embryos appeared grossly normal and expression of Nkx2.5 was intact in the heart at E9.5.
source: Bmp7R-GFlag/- embryos appeared grossly normal (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G–J), and expression of the BMP target gene Nkx2.5, was intact in the heart at E9.5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G'–J').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: By E10.5, all four Bmp7R-GFlag/- embryos that were analyzed were smaller and their hearts showed a common atrium, small right ventricle, small malformed OFT and reduced expression of Nkx2.5.
source: By E10.5, however, all four Bmp7R-GFlag/- embryos that were analyzed were smaller (Figure 5P) and their hearts showed a common atrium (CA), small right ventricle (RV), small malformed OFT and reduced expression of Nkx2.5 (Figure 5P') relative to siblings (Figure 5M–O').
evidence: This is supported by observational data and images shown in Figure 5.

claim: Compound mutants heterozygous for the control Bmp7Flag allele in combination with Bmp2-/+, Bmp4-/+ or Bmp7-/+ were adult viable and showed no gross phenotypic defects.
source: By contrast, compound mutants heterozygous for the control Bmp7Flag allele in combination with Bmp2-/+, Bmp4-/+ or Bmp7-/+ were adult viable and showed no gross phenotypic defects (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by breeding data shown in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Heterodimers consisting of BMP7 together with BMP2 and/or BMP4 are essential for many early developmental processes including ventral body wall closure and formation of the heart.
source: Collectively, these findings suggest that heterodimers consisting of BMP7 together with BMP2 and/or BMP4 are essential for many early developmental processes including ventral body wall closure and formation of the heart.
evidence: This is inferred from the compound heterozygote phenotypic data.

claim: Other class II BMPs cannot fully compensate for BMP7 in the heterodimer pool in the heart.
source: In addition, other class II BMPs cannot fully compensate for BMP7 in the heterodimer pool in the heart.
evidence: This is inferred from the Bmp7R-GFlag/- phenotypic data.

claim: Bands that co-migrate with the BMP4 precursor protein and the lower band in the cleaved mature BMP4 doublet were detected in Flag immunoprecipitates from Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos, but not from wild type littermates.
source: In Flag immunoprecipitates, bands that co-migrate with the BMP4 precursor protein and the lower band in the cleaved mature BMP4 doublet were detected in lysates from Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos, but not from wild type littermates (Figure 6A, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblot data shown in Figure 6.

claim: A band of the appropriate size for the BMP7R-GFlag precursor protein was detected in immunoprecipitates from Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos, but not from wild type littermates.
source: A band of the appropriate size for the BMP7R-GFlag precursor protein was detected in immunoprecipitates from Bmp7R-GFlag/+ embryos, but not from wild type littermates (Figure 6A, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblot data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Bands of the appropriate size for the BMP4 precursor protein and cleaved mature were detected in Flag immunoprecipitates from Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos, but not from wild type littermates.
source: As shown in Figure 6B, when immunoblots of immunoprecipitates were probed with BMP4 antibodies, bands of the appropriate size for the BMP4 precursor protein and cleaved mature were detected in lysates from Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos, but not from wild type littermates (left panel).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblot data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Bands of the appropriate size for the BMP7Flag precursor protein and cleaved mature ligand were detected in immunoprecipitates from Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos, but not from wild type littermates.
source: Bands of the appropriate size for the BMP7Flag precursor protein and cleaved mature ligand were detected in immunoprecipitates from Bmp7Flag/Flag embryos, but not from wild type littermates (Figure 6B, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblot data shown in Figure 6.

claim: BMP2/7 and/or BMP4/7 heterodimers are the predominant functional signaling ligand in many tissues of early mouse embryos.
source: The current studies demonstrate that BMP2/7 and/or BMP4/7 heterodimers are the predominant functional signaling ligand in many tissues of early mouse embryos.
evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from all the genetic and biochemical data presented.

claim: BMP activity is intact in the eye field of Bmp7 null mutants at E9.5.
source: BMP activity is intact in the eye field of Bmp7 null mutants at E9.5, but is absent in Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes, suggesting that BMP7-containing heterodimers play an essential role in early inductive events in the eye.
evidence: This is inferred from the BRE-LacZ reporter data shown in Figure 3.

claim: BMP activity is absent in the eye field of Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes at E9.5.
source: BMP activity is intact in the eye field of Bmp7 null mutants at E9.5, but is absent in Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes, suggesting that BMP7-containing heterodimers play an essential role in early inductive events in the eye.
evidence: This is supported by BRE-LacZ reporter data shown in Figure 3.

claim: BMP7-containing heterodimers play an essential role in early inductive events in the eye.
source: BMP activity is intact in the eye field of Bmp7 null mutants at E9.5, but is absent in Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes, suggesting that BMP7-containing heterodimers play an essential role in early inductive events in the eye.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential BMP activity in Bmp7 null versus Bmp7R-GFlag mutants.

claim: Bmp4 and Bmp7 are co-expressed in head surface ectoderm at the time of lens placode induction (E9).
source: Bmp4 and Bmp7 are co-expressed in head surface ectoderm at the time of lens placode induction (E9), and both have been implicated in this process (Dudley and Robertson, 1997; Furuta and Hogan, 1998; Wawersik et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Both Bmp4 and Bmp7 have been implicated in lens placode induction.
source: Bmp4 and Bmp7 are co-expressed in head surface ectoderm at the time of lens placode induction (E9), and both have been implicated in this process (Dudley and Robertson, 1997; Furuta and Hogan, 1998; Wawersik et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: BMP6 can rescue eye defects in Bmp7 null mutants, whereas BMP4 cannot.
source: Analysis of embryos engineered to express Bmp4 or Bmp6 from the Bmp7 allele demonstrates that BMP6 can rescue eye defects in Bmp7 null mutants, whereas BMP4 cannot (Oxburgh et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The higher specific activity of endogenous BMP4/7 heterodimers is essential to generate sufficient BMP activity for lens induction.
source: This finding is consistent with the possibility that the higher specific activity of endogenous BMP4/7 heterodimers is essential to generate sufficient BMP activity for lens induction.
evidence: This is speculated based on the rescue experiments and heterodimer activity data.

claim: The role of BMP4/7 heterodimers in eye development is likely conserved in humans.
source: The role of BMP4/7 heterodimers in eye development is likely conserved in humans since Bmp4 or Bmp7 are co-expressed in the developing human eye, and mutations in either gene are associated with anophthalmia, microphthalmia and chorioretinal coloboma (Bakrania et al., 2008; Wyatt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is inferred from human genetic data and expression patterns supported by citations.

claim: Bmp4 or Bmp7 are co-expressed in the developing human eye.
source: The role of BMP4/7 heterodimers in eye development is likely conserved in humans since Bmp4 or Bmp7 are co-expressed in the developing human eye, and mutations in either gene are associated with anophthalmia, microphthalmia and chorioretinal coloboma (Bakrania et al., 2008; Wyatt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Mutations in either Bmp4 or Bmp7 are associated with anophthalmia, microphthalmia and chorioretinal coloboma in humans.
source: The role of BMP4/7 heterodimers in eye development is likely conserved in humans since Bmp4 or Bmp7 are co-expressed in the developing human eye, and mutations in either gene are associated with anophthalmia, microphthalmia and chorioretinal coloboma (Bakrania et al., 2008; Wyatt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to human genetic studies.

claim: Point mutations within the prodomain of BMP4 or BMP7 are associated with an overlapping spectrum of brain and palate abnormalities in humans.
source: Point mutations within the prodomain of BMP4 or BMP7 are also associated with an overlapping spectrum of brain and palate abnormalities (Bakrania et al., 2008; Suzuki et al., 2009; Wyatt et al., 2010; Reis et al., 2011), and several of these lead to single amino acid substitutions within short regions of the prodomain that are highly conserved between BMP4 and BMP7.
evidence: This is supported by citations to human genetic studies.

claim: Several point mutations in the prodomain of BMP4 or BMP7 lead to single amino acid substitutions within short regions of the prodomain that are highly conserved between BMP4 and BMP7.
source: Point mutations within the prodomain of BMP4 or BMP7 are also associated with an overlapping spectrum of brain and palate abnormalities (Bakrania et al., 2008; Suzuki et al., 2009; Wyatt et al., 2010; Reis et al., 2011), and several of these lead to single amino acid substitutions within short regions of the prodomain that are highly conserved between BMP4 and BMP7.
evidence: This is supported by citations to human genetic studies.

claim: The prodomain of BMP4 is both necessary and sufficient to generate heterodimeric BMP4/7 ligands.
source: We have shown that the prodomain of BMP4 is both necessary and sufficient to generate heterodimeric BMP4/7 ligands (Neugebauer et al., 2015), raising the possibility that the amino acid substitutions interfere with heterodimer formation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Amino acid substitutions in the prodomain may interfere with heterodimer formation.
source: We have shown that the prodomain of BMP4 is both necessary and sufficient to generate heterodimeric BMP4/7 ligands (Neugebauer et al., 2015), raising the possibility that the amino acid substitutions interfere with heterodimer formation.
evidence: This is speculated based on the role of the prodomain in heterodimer formation.

claim: The heart defects observed in Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes appear earlier (by E9.5) but otherwise phenocopy those in Bmp7R-GFlag/+;Bmp4-/+ and Bmp7R-GFlag/- mutants.
source: The heart defects observed in Bmp7R-GFlag homozygotes appear earlier (by E9.5) but otherwise phenocopy those in Bmp7R-GFlag/+;Bmp4-/+ and Bmp7R-GFlag/- mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparative phenotypic analysis shown in Figures 2 and 5.

claim: BMP4/7 heterodimers play essential roles in early stages of heart development that cannot be compensated for by other BMP family members.
source: This suggests that BMP4/7 heterodimers play essential roles in early stages of heart development that cannot be compensated for by other BMP family members.
evidence: This is inferred from the heart defects in compound heterozygotes.

claim: BMP4 is essential for septation of the ventricles, atrioventricular canal and outflow tract, as well as for valve formation and remodeling of the branchial arch arteries.
source: BMP4 is essential for septation of the ventricles, atrioventricular canal and outflow tract, as well as for valve formation and remodeling of the branchial arch arteries (Jiao et al., 2003; Liu et al., 2004; McCulley et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: BMP2 is not able to compensate for BMP4 during early heart development.
source: Although BMP2 is not able to compensate for BMP4 during early heart development, our finding that Bmp7R-GFlag/+;Bmp2-/+ compound heterozygotes have defects in the heart and in ventral body wall closure that phenocopy those observed in Bmp2;Bmp4 compound heterozygotes (Goldman et al., 2009; Uchimura et al., 2009) suggest that BMP2 and BMP4 function redundantly as heterodimeric partners with BMP7 later in development.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic data and supported by citations.

claim: BMP2 and BMP4 function redundantly as heterodimeric partners with BMP7 later in development.
source: Although BMP2 is not able to compensate for BMP4 during early heart development, our finding that Bmp7R-GFlag/+;Bmp2-/+ compound heterozygotes have defects in the heart and in ventral body wall closure that phenocopy those observed in Bmp2;Bmp4 compound heterozygotes (Goldman et al., 2009; Uchimura et al., 2009) suggest that BMP2 and BMP4 function redundantly as heterodimeric partners with BMP7 later in development.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic similarity between different compound heterozygotes.

claim: Bmp7 null mutants do not show defects in heart development.
source: While Bmp7 null mutants do not show defects in heart development, conditional deletion of both Bmp7 and Bmp4 from progenitors of the secondary heart field leads to persistent truncus arteriosus (Bai et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by observational data from this study and citation to prior research.

claim: Conditional deletion of both Bmp7 and Bmp4 from progenitors of the secondary heart field leads to persistent truncus arteriosus.
source: While Bmp7 null mutants do not show defects in heart development, conditional deletion of both Bmp7 and Bmp4 from progenitors of the secondary heart field leads to persistent truncus arteriosus (Bai et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Heart defects from conditional deletion of Bmp7 and Bmp4 may be due in part to reduction in the BMP4/7 and BMP2/7 heterodimer pool.
source: Collectively, our results raise the possibility that these defects are due in part to reduction in the BMP4/7 and BMP2/7 heterodimer pool, rather than the loss of functionally redundant BMP4 and BMP7 homodimers.
evidence: This is speculated based on the heterodimer model and the phenotypic data.

claim: Endogenous BMP activity is intact in the roof plate of the spinal cord in Bmp7 null mutants at E9.5.
